name: Yvonne and Yvon

sources: Luzel, F. M. Celtic Folk-Tales from Amorica. Translated by Derek Bryce. Dyfed, Wales: Llanerch Enterprises, 1985. Pages 7-18.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: A folktale of Brittany, likely Celtic in origin, tells of Yvonne and her brother Yvon. The sun saw Yvonne's beauty, diligence, and patience. One day he carried her away to the sky where he dwelled. A year passed and the family heard nothing more of her. Yvon walked toward the western horizon with his five brothers. They hoped to reach the sun's domain. Many adventures followed and the brothers grew discouraged. Yvon alone pressed on through trials until he found his sister. She lived happily in the sun's house. When Yvon returned home, ages had passed. Every trace of his family had vanished from the land.

okr.objective: Yvonne and Yvon is a Breton folktale of a maiden carried off by the sun.
key_results: The sun carried off Yvonne for her beauty, diligence, and patience.
Yvon and his five brothers walked toward the western horizon to find her.
Yvon alone reached the sun's house, where his sister lived happily.
When Yvon returned home, ages had passed and all memory of his family was gone.
